1969 Plymouth Road Runner Has It All: Restored, 426 Hemi, 1-of-1 Status
19 photos
Photo: Mecum Auctions
In 1968, Plymouth had three B-body cars in showrooms. In addition to the bread-and-butter Belvedere, it also offered the premium Satellite and the GTX. The latter was an upscale muscle car. That year, it introduced the Road Runner as its fourth intermediate.
The latter filled another gap between the Belvedere and the GTX. It was similar to the latter, as in it was restricted to two-door body styles and big-block V8 engines. However, it lacked the GTX's premium features and came standard with the 383-cubic-inch (6.3-liter) V8. The GTX featured the larger 440-cubic-inch (7.2-liter) RB in base form.
The lack of fancy features and the standard 383 V8 made the Road Runner notably more affordable than the GTX. As a result, it was also far more popular. Plymouth sold over 44,000 examples in 1968 alone, more than the total GTX production between 1967 and 1971. In 1969, Road Runner sales reached an all-time high with over 81,000 examples delivered.
This number makes the 1969 Road Runner one of the most common muscle cars from the golden era. However, that changes when the standard 383-cubic-inch V8 is replaced with any of the optional powertrains. In 1969, the list included both the 440-cubic-inch (7.2-liter) Six-Barrel and the 426-cubic-inch (7.0-liter) Hemi.
The former was brand-new for 1969 and included in the A12 package. The bundle had several heavy-duty items that turned the Road Runner into a drag-ready vehicle. Only 1,412 units were ordered with the A12 package.
The Hemi was carried over from 1968 and found its way into far fewer examples. Records show that 787 examples were fitted with the 425-horsepower V8. The number is split between 421 hardtops, 356 coupes, and 10 convertibles. A little more than half of these cars got the four-speed manual , with the others equipped with the three-speed TorqueFlite automatic.
The stunning Mopar you see here is one of those rigs ordered with the desirable four-speed manual gearbox. It's one of 234 hardtops fitted with the Hemi/manual setup and a one-of-one gem due to its color and trim combo. This Road Runner is a very formal car finished in black and with white upholstery. It also has a bench front seat.
The hardtop appears to be in amazing condition, which isn't surprising given that it was restored on a rotisserie in 2013. Moreover, it was stripped down to bare metal and repainted earlier in 2026. It has a numbers-matching drivetrain, and it's a Super Track Pak model with a Dana 60 rear end with 4.10 gears.
The Mopar was recently added to the lots of Mecum's Kissimmee 2027 auction , which takes place in January. It's one of 17 Hemi-powered classics scheduled to cross the block at the event, and it will change hands for a six-figure sum. I'm pretty sure it will sell for over $200,000.
